title: ODOC-437 slice 2: the lean task-startup pack -- purpose, criteria, dependency artifacts and source anchors only (AC2)
description:
ODOC-437 slice 2. Advances AC2. Design of record: docs/specs/opum-task-context-and-evidence-contract.md in opum-doc (origin/dev).

REUSE; define nothing new (leader ruling Q2). The spec TaskContract already carries `dependencies` (taskId, revision, satisfied -- Quest dependencies) and `documentation` (repositoryId, conceptId, optional anchor, relation -- Quest documentation links). Selection step 2: "Seed from task links. Read mandatory anchors first. Prefer a stable section reference to a whole long spec." A missing MANDATORY reference is CONTEXT_REQUIRED_SOURCE_MISSING; a missing OPTIONAL one is an omission with a reason.

Deliverable: the lean task-startup pack. Depends on Slice 1 (LCLI-680). Keep the two path-disjoint: put the selection change in retrieval (Slice 1) and this startup shape in the agent-context compilation path (Slice 2).

acceptanceCriteria.text: A task startup pack contains purpose, acceptance criteria, dependency artifacts and necessary source anchors, and contains NO full task notes, fleet backlogs or parent transcripts.
Expansion reads exact sections by concept and anchor on demand.
A missing mandatory reference fails with CONTEXT_REQUIRED_SOURCE_MISSING; a missing optional one is an omission carrying a reason.

plan: Ground in the design of record: opum-doc docs/specs/opum-task-context-and-evidence-contract.md (origin/dev), TaskContract + selection steps 1-2 + pack format.

Hydrate the Quest task through its PUBLIC interface before compiling: read purpose, acceptance criteria, dependencies (taskId, revision, satisfied) and documentation links (repositoryId, conceptId, optional anchor, relation); validate the envelope and capture the revision. REUSE the spec TaskContract fields; define nothing new (leader ruling Q2). Passing the task id as --task TEXT is not sufficient hydration.
Build the lean task-startup pack shape: purpose, acceptance criteria, dependency artifacts and necessary source anchors ONLY -- no full task notes, no fleet backlogs, no parent transcripts (AC1).
Expansion: exact-section reads by concept and anchor on demand (AC2).
Missing MANDATORY reference -> fail CONTEXT_REQUIRED_SOURCE_MISSING; missing OPTIONAL -> an omission carrying a reason (AC3).
Keep this path-disjoint from Slice 1 (LCLI-680): put the selection change in retrieval, this startup shape in the agent-context compilation path.
Tests + gates: bun test, bun run lore check, typecheck, lint.
implementationNotes: LCLI-681 claimed and grounded (branch feat/LCLI-681-lean-task-startup-pack). Read the design of record, opum-doc docs/specs/opum-task-context-and-evidence-contract.md at origin/dev (20,373 bytes), fetched over the GitHub API because the DEC-158 ownership guard blocks reading a sibling checkout. Scope confirmed large: src/core/agent-context.ts is 1,353 lines and today the task reaches the compiler as free TEXT (agent.ts resolveTask), so AC1 needs genuine Quest-task HYDRATION (purpose, acceptance criteria, dependencies, documentation links) before the lean pack can carry them -- a new integration, not a reshape. No product code written yet; the claim is the only commit on the branch. Queued behind LCLI-685 (Done) and LCLI-660 (Done).

HANDOFF FOR PR 2 (written 2026-10-06). PR 1 is LANDED; LCLI-681 stays In Progress until PR 2 lands, per the leader-approved two-PR split.

PR 1 — DELIVERED. PR opum-ai/lore-cli#501, squash 1604bc4f. Adds `--task-contract <repo-relative-path|->` on `lore agent context <profile>`, taking a controller-composed TaskContract/v1 and compiling the lean task-startup pack. Covers AC1 (purpose, acceptance criteria and dependency artifacts in the pack; the contract's `documentation` links seeded as pins, preferring the link's anchor; nothing from task notes/backlog/transcript) and AC3 (a missing MANDATORY link — requires/constrains — fails with CONTEXT_REQUIRED_SOURCE_MISSING on stderr and a nonzero exit; a missing OPTIONAL one — explains/verifies — is an omission carrying its reason and the compile still succeeds). New files: src/core/task-contract.ts (the parser, the marker, the mandatory/optional split) and test/lcli681-task-contract-startup-pack.test.ts (9 cases). `--task` keeps its meaning; `--task-contract` is exclusive with it, with the binding seam, and with `--workspace`.

PR 1's REVIEW found and I fixed two real defects in the anchor seam (546e830d): an OPTIONAL link with a stale ANCHOR hard-failed instead of being omitted (F1), and a MANDATORY one failed without the marker (F2). `anchorResolves()` in src/core/agent-context.ts is the shared non-throwing predicate; the contract loop now checks concept AND anchor together. Three tests cover that dimension.

PR 2 — STILL TO DO: AC2, "Expansion reads exact sections by concept and anchor on demand."

THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES IT. `lore read <id>` is the existing exact-read surface and its own docstring makes an invariant of returning the WHOLE concept — "no budget flag at all ... no configuration under which it returns less than the whole concept" — and it has no anchor support. So AC2 cannot be done by quietly widening `lore read`; that invariant has to be preserved or explicitly renegotiated with opum-doc.

THE A/B PUT TO THE LEADER (2026-10-06), recommendation first:
- A (recommended): a NEW anchor-addressed exact read, `lore read <id> --anchor <slug>` (or the `<id>#<slug>` spelling the pack's link `normalized` already uses), returning exactly that section with `lore read`'s existing provenance shape; the default stays the whole concept. Reuses `anchorResolves` rather than a second resolution. Matches the spec's "users can open exact sources without invoking a model" and "an explicit, bounded expansion".
- B: an expansion flag on `lore agent context` itself (`--expand <concept>#<anchor>`) that widens the startup pack. Rejected as the recommendation because it makes the pack the expansion surface and spends pack budget where the spec calls for a bounded exact read.

SECOND CONSTRAINT, live and easy to trip: the `implementation` agent profile declares BOTH `docs/reference/cli-surface.md` and `docs/specs/agent-profile-context-retrieval.md` as sources, and after PR 1's documentation additions its budget margin is essentially ZERO (the reviewer measured 12 tokens before, and PR 1 consumed nearly all of it). ANY further edit to a declared source can fire the `agent-profile-capacity` finding, which becomes an ERROR once LCLI-646's DEC-11 flip lands. Measure with `bun run lore check` after any doc touch, and expect to trim. This is LCLI-682's reshape territory.

STATE AT HANDOFF. dev == origin/dev == 1604bc4f. No open PRs. No stray branches. LCLI-681 In Progress. Next after LCLI-681: LCLI-658 (win32-x64 carve-out) per the leader's 2026-10-06 message, then LCLI-682 and LCLI-683. LCLI-665 stays parked.

LCLI-681 PR 2 — RULING RECORDED (2026-10-06), so a successor builds it. DEC-163 (5c) (opum-doc; its record was still travelling to opum-doc dev when this was written — re-read it there before starting). The decision chose option A of the A/B below, NARROWED to one spelling. Do NOT build this in the session that recorded it.

THE SURFACE, exactly: `lore read <id>#<slug>` — the `<id>#<slug>` spelling the agent-context pack's link `normalized` already emits, so the two surfaces name a section identically. There is NO `--anchor` alias; one spelling only.

BEHAVIOUR:
- It returns EXACTLY that section, carrying the provenance shape `lore read` already emits (`id`, `path`, `type`, `frontmatter`, `body`, `tokenEstimate`) — not a new envelope.
- A missing anchor is a `validation` error that NAMES THE REPAIR (mirror the existing anchor diagnostic: correct the anchor, or drop the `#anchor` to read the whole document).
- It REUSES PR 1's anchor resolution — `anchorResolves()` in src/core/agent-context.ts — and must not grow a second implementation of the same predicate. That function is currently module-private; exporting it (or lifting it to a shared module) is part of this work.
- It NEVER invokes a model. The exact read is a direct filesystem load, exactly as the whole-concept form is.

THE INVARIANT AMENDMENT, required: `lore read <id>` with no anchor still returns the whole concept, unchanged. Amend the invariant its docstring states — it currently reads "no budget flag at all … no configuration under which it returns less than the whole concept" — to: "returns the whole concept unless the caller names one section by anchor; no budget flag and no configuration ever returns less than what was named." That sentence is the only part of `lore read`'s stated contract this change touches; preserve the rest.

B IS REJECTED — do not put the expansion on `lore agent context` (no `--expand` flag), and do not spend pack budget for a read.

DOCS AND THE BUDGET CONSTRAINT: the `implementation` agent profile declares BOTH `docs/reference/cli-surface.md` and `docs/specs/agent-profile-context-retrieval.md` as sources, and after PR 1 its budget margin is essentially ZERO (the PR 1 reviewer measured 12 tokens before PR 1's own additions). Any documentation this change needs must FIT that margin by trimming, measured with `bun run lore check` reading 0 warnings — or it WAITS for LCLI-682, which reshapes these budgets. Do NOT raise `implementation.max_tokens` ad hoc.

PR 1 IS LANDED, so the successor starts from a green dev, not from scratch: PR opum-ai/lore-cli#501, squash 1604bc4f, plus the PR 2 handoff itself. The A/B that led to the ruling is in the previous note on this task; the reviewer's F1/F2 anchor-seam defects were fixed in 546e830d and the anchor dimension now has test coverage (test/lcli681-task-contract-startup-pack.test.ts, 9 cases).
